# The Raptor's Talon

*Page PDF 10*

THE CORSAIRS OF CAPTAIN FL ARIEL 

## **The Raptor’s Talon**
Flariel’s vessel is a ravenship. These are the most common warships in Druchii fleets and the _Raptor’s Talon_ is typical of its class. The hull is carved with graceful lines and protruding spikes, with timbers painted as black as the sails. At the prow, twin figureheads represent Sea Dragons, while spiked crenellations protect the aftcastle. The two masts fly Flariel’s heraldry (a fanged mouth with crossed hooks), the home port of Karond Kar (a daggerwielding harpy), and the personal insignia of Duriath Helbane (a serpentine Helldrake). 

The _Raptor’s Talon_ mounts two batteries of Reapers on either side. These are ballistae which fire multiple bolts in swift succession. Use the profile on page 100 of **Sea of Claws** and add the Salvo (6) Quality.

## **Uniform**
Corsairs wear cloaks fashioned from Sea Dragon hide, with mufflers and thick clothes to keep out the freezing sea winds. Flariel’s Reavers favour deep marine green and grey fabrics. Each corsair wields cutlasses, punch daggers, and repeating hand crossbows. 

Flariel is smart enough to raid only targets he can defeat — if numbers and superior Dark Elf tactics make victory unlikely, he withdraws. During an assault, rather than overwhelming numbers, the Elves make use of their speed and agility to surprise and outmanoeuvre their enemies. Once an opponent’s fighters are dead or suppressed, Corvian rounds up survivors and escorts them by boat to the _Raptor’s Talon_ . 

## **Shield Design**
Corsairs are agile fighters who engage in boarding actions and swift assaults. They carry two weapons rather than a shield. 

## **Battlecry**
Flariel’s Reavers do not cry out in battle, preferring to hiss prayers to Khaine and Mathlann as they close with the enemy. 

## **Tactics**
Flariel’s Reavers employ stealth and darkness when attacking adversaries. They use their Night Vision as an advantage over Humans and relish the fear they cause by slipping swiftly from the gloom towards their prey. 

When attacking a coastal settlement, Captain Flariel deploys a scouting force to explore the lie of the land. This includes several corsairs accompanying the most perceptive sailors from the crew. They ascertain the best routes for attack and opportunistically kill anyone they encounter, providing it doesn’t alert the populace. When Flariel feels bored or capricious, he joins the scouting party himself. 

At sea, the _Raptor’s Talon_ attacks vulnerable shipping with the same principles — stealth and speed. Rakaria may summon a sea mist to conceal the ship’s approach, before the helmsman sweeps the Druchii vessel into close quarters, while the crew rake the enemy with reaper fire. On closing, Captain Flariel orders the grappling hooks and boarding ramp deployed, allowing the corsairs to board the enemy vessel and kill all they find. If the other ship receives the attack with cannon fire, the _Raptor’s Talon_ sweeps away to escape before pouncing once again from the mist. 

## Splinter by Splinter
Drok Greyhammer does not complain about his situation, not even to his fellow Dwarf captives. He rows, he eats his meagre rations, and he snatches sleep whenever he can. Despair has given Drok complete focus on one activity — scraping a hole in the hold of the Raptor’s Talon to take himself and all others on board to a watery grave. Each day, he reaches below his bench and scratches a few splinters away with the handle of a broken spoon that he keeps hidden underneath his bench. It has taken years, and now the wood is weakening. If the other captives discover Drok’s obsession, will they help, or tell Corvian in order to save their own lives?
